title: Ralph Ellison's birth chart
metaDescription: Ralph Ellison's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 10.3° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, Mercury holds a trine to Neptune at 1.0° — close enough to weld thinking to imagination. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 10.3° of Pisces is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by the Moon in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Pisces (24.8°), Venus in Pisces (14.7°), Mars in Cancer (7.3°): thought steeped in tone and memory, attraction that works by atmosphere, effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Jupiter to Uranus, a conjunction with 0.4° of slack. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line. Behind it, Mercury trine Neptune at 1.0°, and the Sun square Saturn at 1.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags three placements in this chart. Mercury in Pisces at 24.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 14.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Cancer at 7.3° is in fall. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: water 5, air 4 across the elements, and mutable 5, cardinal 2, fixed 2 across the modalities. No settled placement falls in fire or earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde. Mercury changed direction during the day, so its motion is left open.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.8° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
